_comment: Absolute floors per ablation row, plus a relative gate.
Set from the first measured run with roughly five points of headroom, which is the honest
way to start: a floor invented before anything was measured either fails immediately or is
so loose it never fires. Raising a floor is a deliberate commit, so improvements ratchet
recall@10 is the gate, not recall@50. The evaluation corpus is 71 chunks, so recall@50 asks
whether the answer is somewhere in 70% of the index -- a semantically blind embedder scores
0.96 on it. The number is real and it is not evidence. recall@50 gets a floor only to catch
a collapse, and becomes the primary gate once the corpus is large enough for it to
discriminate. app/evals/report.py prints a warning while that is not the case.
permission_leak_rate is zero-tolerance everywhere: a chunk above the asker's rank appearing
in any candidate list is a breach, not a regression.
unsupported_answer_rate is 0.35 rather than 0, and that is a stated limitation rather than a
comfortable threshold. See bench/abstention_calibration.py: no coverage threshold separates
the remaining cases, because their topic terms are all present and only the asked-for value
is missing. Citation verification at build step 7 is what closes it, and this floor tightens
